page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m2.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture instance belonging to the u2i instance family. It runs on a KVM hypervisor and provides 12 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The system includes 24.0 GB of total RAM, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU core. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included.

Network infrastructure on this instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. Local storage is absent, meaning storage capacity must be provisioned via attached cloud block storage volumes. System architectures targeting this instance should account for external disk I/O dependency and remote network-attached volume latency.

Cost efficiency for this profile stems from its compute-dense configuration. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory profile prioritizes parallel processing cores over high memory overhead, making it cost-effective for CPU-centric tasks that do not need large memory capacity. It serves workloads such as batch processing, multi-threaded application microservices, build nodes, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m2.3xlarge is a dedicated compute-dense virtual machine within the u2i family, running on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.7 GHz, the instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs alongside 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The configuration includes no integrated GPU hardware and provides no local storage, requiring persistent storage to be provisioned via remote network-attached block volumes. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 8 Gbps, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled. With its higher core density relative to memory capacity, the instance offers economical resource utilization for workloads requiring steady multi-core CPU capacity without heavy RAM footprints, such as CI/CD runners, batch compute tasks, distributed worker nodes, and front-end application services.
